In this regard, criminal case was registered by Electronic City Traffic Police against him, in Crime No.146/2023 for the offences punishable under section 279, 304(A) of IPC.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to the notice, respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed written statements.
6. In the written statement the respondent No.1 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

It is also contention of the respondent No.1 that accident was not occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself and not on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-53-C-9438.
Further, stated that, he is the RC Owner of the car bearing registration No.KA-53-C-9438 and the said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and policy was in force as on the date of the accident.

Hence, he prayed to dismiss the petition against the respondent No.2 .
7.
In the written statement the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing registration No.KA-53-C-9438 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further it has stated that, the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of the accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
It is the defence of the respondent No.2 that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself and not on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-53-C- 9438.

Further respondent No.2 has denied the age,
avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.

It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive,
exhorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

Consequently, Janson Francis died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.

15. On the other hand, the respondents denied about the involvement of the offending in the alleged accident and contended that, said vehicle is falsely implicated in the accident in order to get compensation.

16. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
17. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name Divya N. examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.

On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Ramachandragowda, PSI, the S.H.O. of Electronic City Traffic Police has registered the case against the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-53-C-9438 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 304(A) of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against driver of the car by name Anand R. alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
19.

The respondents have taken the contention that the accident was not occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-53-C-9438 as car was proceeding in the extreme left side of the road, in slow manner and the deceased being the rider of the motor cycle rode the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the car.
But the respondents failed to examine either the driver of the offending vehicle or any independent eye witness to prove their contention.
Though, the respondent No.2 has examined its Assistant Manager of the Insurance Company as RW1, but his evidence will not much helpful to prove the contention of the respondents.

20. Apart from this, at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.2 about the denial of allegation made against the driver of Divya N vs Gowrisha D.S on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5446799/

21. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-53-C- 9438 and in the said accident, Janson Francis succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly,
I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative and the additional issue No.1 is in the Negative.

ISSUE No.2:
22.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P14 to Ex.P18 and Ex.P27 to Ex.P29 Aadhar cards of the petitioners, marriage certificate, birth certificates of petitioner No.2 & 3 have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

23. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 being the wife has lost her husband and the petitioner No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased have lost their love and affection of their father, petitioner No.4 & 5 are the parents have lost their son, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
24. The petitioners herein, have placed driving licence card marked at Ex.P13 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 29.7.1992.
The accident occurred on 19.4.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 31 years.
For his age, multiplier '16' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.

Bengaluru and was drawing salary of Rs.38,000/- per month.

After deducting professional tax at Rs.200/- it comes to Rs.29,439/- per month.

27. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"

entities.text: 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "

28. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
29. In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are five persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
30. In the present case, deceased was aged about 31 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "16" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was under below 40 years, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.29,439/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.3,53,268/- per year.

Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.3,53,268+1,41,307) =
Rs.4,94,575/-.
And 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.3,70,931.25(Rs.4,94,575-Rs.1,23,643.75).
This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "16" which comes to Rs.59,34,900/-.

2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Additional Issue No.2 :
35.

The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that the driver of the car bearing No.KA-53-C-9438 had no valid and effective driving licence and had no permit and fitness Divya N vs Gowrisha D.S on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5446799/
8 certificate to the vehicle to ply in the public place.
Though the respondent No.2 has examined its Assistant Mahager as RW1.
He has placed extract of diving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
On perusal of the same, it is clear that driver of the offending vehicle had licence to drive non-transport from 28.10.2021 to 27.10.2031.
Hence, it is crystal clear that as on the date of accident driver had valid and effective driving licence.
Further respondent has not placed any documents to show that the offending vehicle had no permit and fitness certificate.
From the documents available on record goes to show that the respondent No.2 had failed to prove that the respondent No.1 had violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, Additional issue No.1 is answered in the Negative.

LIABILITY:
36.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-53-C-9438,
alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
37. As per Ex.R2 insurance policy was valid from 8.7.2022 to 7.7.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 19.4.2023.
As such, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
38.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for  compensation of Rs.61,87,900/- (Rupees sixtyone lakh eighty seven thousand and nine hundred only) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for the share of 50%, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled the share of 20% each and the petitioner No.4 & 5 are entitled the share of 5% each.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- for the death of Mr.Janson Francis in a road traffic accident.
In this regard, criminal case was registered by Electronic City Traffic Police against him, in Crime No.146/2023 for the offences punishable under section 279, 304(A) of IPC.
opennyai_summary.issue:
8. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
Divya N vs Gowrisha D.S on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5446799/
3 ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that Janson Francis had died in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 19-04- 2023 at about 4-10 p.m. near Hosuru main road, Elevated Flyover Pillar No.173, Pragathinagar,
Electronic City, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-53-C- 9438 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, at what rate and from whom?
3) What order or award?
Additional Issues:
1) Whether the respondent No.2 proves that this accident is due to the rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle by the deceased himself?
2. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that respondent No.1 has violated the fundamental conditions of the policy as stated at the para No.12 & 13 of the written statement?
14. It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-53-C-9438, the alleged accident had taken place.
16. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle in question.
opennyai_summary.arguments: 15. On the other hand, the respondents denied about the involvement of the offending in the alleged accident and contended that, said vehicle is falsely implicated in the accident in order to get compensation.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against driver of the car by name Anand R. alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
19.
Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 29.7.1992.
28. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
30. In the present case, deceased was aged about 31 years as on the date of the accident.
And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was under below 40 years, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
On perusal of the same, it is clear that driver of the offending vehicle had licence to drive non-transport from 28.10.2021 to 27.10.2031.
Hence, it is crystal clear that as on the date of accident driver had valid and effective driving licence.
Further respondent has not placed any documents to show that the offending vehicle had no permit and fitness certificate.
From the documents available on record goes to show that the respondent No.2 had failed to prove that the respondent No.1 had violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, Additional issue No.1 is answered in the Negative.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The alleged accident had taken place on 19.4.2023.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.29,439/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.3,53,268/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.3,53,268+1,41,307) =
Rs.4,94,575/-.
And 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "16" which comes to Rs.59,34,900/-.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
. Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.61,87,900/-
(Rupees sixtyone lakh eighty seven thousand and nine hundred only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No. 103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
37. As per Ex.R2 insurance policy was valid from 8.7.2022 to 7.7.2023.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
ISSUE No.3:
38.
In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for  compensation of Rs.61,87,900/- (Rupees sixtyone lakh eighty seven thousand and nine hundred only) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for the share of 50%, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled the share of 20% each and the petitioner No.4 & 5 are entitled the share of 5% each.
Divya N vs Gowrisha D.S on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5446799/
9
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1, 4 & 5, 40% of their share shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% of their share shall be released in favour of them through due process of law.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.2 & 3, since they are minors, entire amount shall be deposited in any Nationalised/Scheduled bank till they attain age of majority.
After attaining the age of majority, entire amount shall be released to them through due process of law.
The guardian of the petitioners is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
[ Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
